title: Custom hooks
summary: A custom hook is a function that uses React hooks to package reusable stateful logic.
whenToUse: Use custom hooks when multiple components need the same effect, state, subscription, persistence, or request logic.
do: Start custom hook names with use.
Return the state and functions the component needs.
Keep UI markup in components and reusable logic in hooks.
dont: Do not call custom hooks conditionally.
Do not hide unrelated app behavior inside one large custom hook.

codeSnippets.title: Extract a document title hook
codeSnippets.description: Move reusable effect logic behind a custom hook.
codeSnippets.explanation: Any component can call useWindowTitle without repeating the effect and cleanup details.

codeSnippets.title: Return state from a custom hook
codeSnippets.description: A hook can expose data, loading state, and error state together.
codeSnippets.explanation: The component receives a small API and does not need to know how the hook manages the internal state.

commonMistake: Extracting a custom hook too early before the repeated logic is clear.
interviewQuestion: What problem do custom hooks solve?
interviewAnswer: They let you reuse stateful React logic between components without duplicating effects and state management.

courseReference.notes: The project extracts movie fetching, localStorage persistence, and keyboard handling into custom hooks.

title: localStorage state hook
summary: A localStorage state hook keeps a state value in sync with browser storage.
whenToUse: Use it for small client-side preferences or saved lists that should survive page refreshes.
do: Read localStorage in a lazy useState initializer.
Write to localStorage in an effect when the value changes.
dont: Do not read localStorage directly during every render.
Do not store sensitive data in localStorage.

codeSnippets.title: Persist state to localStorage
codeSnippets.description: Initialize from localStorage once, then write changes in an effect.
codeSnippets.explanation: The lazy initializer avoids reading storage on every render, and the effect persists each value change.

commonMistake: Calling localStorage.getItem directly in the component body on every render.
interviewQuestion: How can you persist React state to localStorage?
interviewAnswer: Initialize state from localStorage with a lazy initializer, then use an effect to write the updated value when it changes.

courseReference.notes: The watched movies list is persisted with a custom localStorage state hook.
